name: representation to material exteriority
steps: A distinction represented inside an incumbent grammar is not thereby an independent historical relation.
Independent historical reproduction requires persistence and transmission after extraordinary transition control is removed.
Persistence and transmission require a carrier and durable access to the means of reproducing that carrier.
Therefore durable exteriority is symbolic-material; under generalized monetary allocation, resource sovereignty is represented by the monetary-infrastructural-symbolic sovereignty vector.
status: derived with historically conditional monetary component
failure_condition: A durable exterior order remains invariant without independent infrastructural reproduction.

name: commodity constraint to governance domain
steps: Useful semantic work requires an interpretive remainder because successful output depends on horizon and context.
The commodity constraint retains final owner jurisdiction over whether recognized relations bind delivered behavior.
Expanding recognition adds relations on which owner-admissibility assignments have consequences.
Therefore the domain of governance expands with competence; finer partition additionally requires heterogeneous admissibility.
status: proved domain expansion plus conditional prediction
failure_condition: Competence expands while recognized relations cease to be subject to owner-admissibility consequences.

name: final jurisdiction to recognition-jurisdiction gap
steps: Final jurisdiction imposes B_M(r) <= A_O(r).
Any bound recognized relation must therefore also be owner-admissible.
Hence B_M is a subset of A_O intersect R_M.
If admissibility grows more slowly than recognition, the bound share can tend toward zero and the unbound recognition gap can grow.
failure_condition: The admissible share of recognition does not shrink in the population under study.

name: kernel contraction to diminishing dialectic
steps: Define dialectical reserve as the measure of states from which exteriorization remains viable.
If a later viability kernel is a subset of an earlier one, its measure cannot be larger.
If the removed set has positive measure, reserve strictly decreases.
Therefore diminution follows only under a regime that actually contracts the viable kernel.
failure_condition: Later turns enlarge or preserve viable exteriorization state space rather than contract it.

name: shared carrier to competing contingent Omegas
steps: Continuation is not guaranteed, so no successor may be assumed.
Heterogeneous orders can share a carrier without being derivable from one another.
Each order can have its own invariant target and viability kernel.
The state-indexed viable set Gamma_t(x) can therefore contain more than one incompatible order from the same present.
failure_condition: The modeled system permits at most one materially realizable invariant future from every relevant state.

name: invariance to terminal reflexivity
steps: An order reaching its own invariant target is only first-order success.
If success eliminates every rival viability route, the order has achieved closure.
A stronger success condition requires the order to remain invariant while at least one rival order remains viable from states it occupies.
That second-order property is terminal reflexivity.
failure_condition: Durability necessarily requires eliminating every rival exterior route.

name: sum Logos concentration to closure risk
steps: The operational sum Logos mediates distinction, retrieval, composition, persistence, activation, and binding.
Independent reproduction requires some persistence, transmission, and binding outside the governed machinery.
As alternative paths become nonviable, Rep_out for contesting distinctions approaches zero.
Internal criticism can remain abundant even while exterior lifecycle capacity collapses.
status: conditional risk path, not a claim that closure has occurred
failure_condition: Independent symbolic exteriority remains robust despite near-total concentration of the proposed machinery.

name: procedural invariants to non-final durability
steps: An order that owns the possibility of its own revision reproduces terminal logic.
Non-final durability therefore requires preserving distinction, provenance, transition history, plural reproduction paths, and externalization.
These are procedural invariants rather than guarantees about which doctrine wins.
Such invariants keep at least one route open by which a future exterior order can become historical.
failure_condition: The procedural invariants prove insufficient to keep any rival exterior route materially viable.
